description: Define logarithms as indices: a^x = b is equivalent to x = log_a(b).
Use the product rule for logarithms: log_a(xy) = log_a(x) + log_a(y).
Use the quotient rule for logarithms: log_a(x/y) = log_a(x) - log_a(y).
Use the power rule for logarithms: log_a(x^k) = k log_a(x).
Interpret a logarithmic scale using L = 10 log_10(I/I_0).
Solve log_a(x) = value by converting to x = a^value.
Define the natural logarithm ln(x) = log_e(x).
Use the inverse relationship between e^x and ln(x), including e^(ln x) = x.
Use d/dx(ln x) = 1/x.
Estimate probabilities from relative frequency count/total.
Calculate continuous probabilities by integrating a probability density function over an interval.
Calculate a cumulative distribution function by integrating the probability density function from the lower support endpoint.
Calculate E(X) = integral of x f(x) dx for a continuous random variable.
Calculate Var(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2.
For Y = aX + b, determine E(Y) = aE(X)+b and SD(Y) = |a|SD(X).
Standardize a normal-distribution value using z = (x-mu)/sigma.
Determine E(p_hat) = p and SD(p_hat) = sqrt(p(1-p)/n).
Standardize a sample proportion using (p_hat-p)/sqrt(p_hat(1-p_hat)/n).
Calculate an approximate confidence interval for a population proportion.
Calculate E = z sqrt(p_hat(1-p_hat)/n).
